q: An echo is repetition of sound due to the reflection of sound. (2024)
e: An echo is formed when sound waves bounce off a reflecting surface back to the listener.

q: Sound travels at different speeds depending on the medium through which it passes. (2024)
e: The speed of sound depends on the density and elasticity of the medium it passes through.

q: The intensity of an echo is less than that of the original sound. (2025)
e: Sound energy is absorbed and spread out as it travels and reflects, reducing the intensity of the echo.

q: An echo is repetition of sound due to the vibration of sound. (2025)
e: An echo is caused by the reflection of sound waves, not vibration.

q: Sound intensity is a direct measure of the energy reaching an ear drum. (2024)
e: Sound intensity measures the rate at which sound energy flows through a unit area perpendicular to the direction of propagation.

q: Ultrasound cannot be heard by human ear. (2024)
e: Ultrasound has a frequency higher than 20,000 Hz, which is above the limit of human hearing.

q: If the amplitude of the sound wave is doubled, the intensity becomes eight times greater. (2025)
e: Sound intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude, so doubling the amplitude increases intensity by four times.

q: Reflection of sound does not obey the laws of reflection. (2021)
e: Reflection of sound obeys the same laws of reflection as light.

q: The speed of sound is higher in liquids than solids. (2021)
e: Sound travels faster in solids than in liquids because solids are more rigid and denser.

q: Echoes can be heard separately from the original sound when the source of the sound is much closer to the observer than to the reflecting surface. (2025)
e: Distinct echoes require sufficient distance to ensure a time delay of at least 0.1 seconds between the original sound and its reflection.

q: The speed of sound is the same for different media. (2021)
e: The speed of sound varies depending on the state and material properties of the medium.

q: The Doppler effect occurs only when the source of sound is moving, not the listener. (2025)
e: The Doppler effect occurs whenever there is relative motion between the source and the listener.

q: The upper limit of audibility is about 200,000 Hz. (2025)
e: The upper limit of human audibility is approximately 20,000 Hz.

q: The intensity of a wave is inversely proportional to the square of the amplitude of the wave. (2025)
e: The intensity of a wave is directly proportional to the square of its amplitude.

q: Sound waves can travel through a vacuum. (2025)
e: Sound waves are mechanical waves and require a medium to propagate; they cannot travel through a vacuum.

q: Doppler ultrasound is a technique that is used to examine blood flow. (2026)
e: Doppler ultrasound measures the reflection of high-frequency sound waves from moving blood cells to evaluate blood flow.
Porous and soft materials effectively absorb sound energy, reducing reverberation and reflection.
